value.identity: The Vigil — the hidden inner ring of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation. Publicly fronted by Aelia Vandros (Executive Director, late fifties, former Senate staffer and war-widow). Operationally architected by Colonel Maro Tess (former senior GAG operations officer, current Greyline Strategic Services strategist, knowing One Sith asset). Mythic recovery agent: Aevyn Soris (28, Jacen Solo's surviving Force student, the side project who lived in the gaps while Ben was Jacen's primary fourteen-year-old apprentice). Mercenary contractors: Greyline (operational arm) and Vara Senn (former Lost Tribe apprentice, archive specialist). Distant: an unnamed One Sith hand.
value.motivation: The Vigil believes the galaxy keeps nearly dying because leaders hesitate, panic, compromise, or wait too long. Jacen failed — but he SAW something real. His unfinished work on Recognition and Holding is, to them, the missing toolkit for clarity, resilience, steadiness, and preparation in the next crisis. They do not call it brainwashing; they call it correction and continuity. Aelia wants the dead to have meant something. Tess wants control because hesitation kills. Aevyn wants to finish the lesson Jacen started with him — and prove he was chosen, not merely useful. The unnamed One Sith hand wants identity-level influence techniques to seed into a broader infiltration program of which Dorvan is a future target, not yet a victim.
value.escalation: Hook (Ch 1): Aevyn Force-interrogates and kills Commander Elya Rane to extract the trail to Jacen's unfinished holocron — precise method, not savage, which makes it worse. PP1 prelude: Greyline runs a procedural-cover snatch at Tarn Velos prison to remove Talon Veyr before Ben can learn enough; Ben breaks cover and rescues him, creating a public legal crisis. PP1 (Ch 14-15): Greyline + Vara Senn hit the GAG archive as a cleanup team, Vara takes Iressa hostage when combat fails, Iressa dies after Ben refuses a Jacen-shaped coercive move. PP2 (Ch 20): the three-part Squeeze — Tess kills Korda as public fall-guy, Iressa's secondary cache is professionally raided and burned (the documentary case for Saba is unrecoverable), and Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime with Tess's tradecraft fingerprint while the Iresh staging accelerates past Ben's planning horizon. Climax (Ch 31-32): Aevyn cracks the cache at the Glasswell; the natural site destabilizes; Tavi and locals are trapped; the duel becomes inevitable. Each escalation compounds across institutional, logistical, and Force dimensions simultaneously.

value.Colonel Maro Tess: Tests the theme as the calm, operational endpoint of crisis logic with no moral counterweight. Treats people as logistics. Survives Book 1 and retreats deeper into One Sith service — proving the system Ben is touching is older and longer than this one operation.
value.Aelia Vandros: Tests the theme as the legible face of the conspiracy: warm, polished, genuinely compassionate, dangerous because much of what she says is true. value.author: Aaron Allston
value.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and dialogue-density reference for Talon Veyr's voice and the Ben/Talon partnership tempo. Emulate: dialogue-forward scene construction; ensemble POV piloting; dry, integrated humor that moves the scene rather than decorates it; political/institutional worldbuilding delivered through argument rather than exposition; prison-and-procedural texture that earns its tension through small physical details (sea wall, storm shutters, camera lag, guard habits); buddy-cop friction that doesn't dilute serious stakes. Benchmark works: Wraith Squadron, Iron Fist, Mercy Kill; Betrayal (LotF book 1) for ensemble POV piloting circa this era.
value.what_to_avoid: Do NOT lean into the comic-relief register when scenes are darkening — the book's Act 3 is genuinely grim and the Talon humor valve must shut. Do NOT copy Allston's chapter-as-vignette structural rhythm; The Unfinished Shadow runs chapters as dramatic units of variable scene count, not Allston-style rotating-cast snapshots. Do NOT imitate his prose as a voice template; the bible forbids author-imitation and Talon must remain a specific character, not 'an Allston wraith'.

value.author: Timothy Zahn
value.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and prose-discipline reference for Colonel Maro Tess's calm operational antagonist register and for Ben Skywalker's POV interiority discipline. Emulate: clean, precise, efficient prose; dialogue that advances plot and reveals character simultaneously; intelligent antagonists who sound intelligent without lecturing; tactical clarity in action scenes; short paragraphs; sentences that do their work and get out of the way. Benchmark works: Heir to the Empire, Specter of the Past as register anchors. Working rule from the Ruusan voice block: 'When in doubt about prose choices, ask whether this sentence would appear in a Zahn novel — if it is ornate or introspective beyond a line or two, the answer is no.'
value.what_to_avoid: Zahn's prose can run emotionally cool — functional rather than felt. Ben's POV needs warmth that Zahn-clear sentences alone do not carry; carry the warmth through behavior, body language, and the small private moments (Ben covering an old GAG sender code before he realizes; Ben taking the half-sandwich from a Civitas coworker; Ben tightening his hand around the table edge when he answers Luke 'Somewhere it can't hurt anyone'). Do NOT import Specter-era political-thriller framing — this is a conspiracy thriller, not a senate-procedural.

value.author: Karen Traviss
value.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and texture reference for the GAG investigation register: institutional and procedural detail handled as CHARACTER rather than as lecture. Emulate: how a former operator narrates logistics, manifests, transfer corrections, and quarantine classifications in the same breath as fear and exhaustion; compressed expert dialogue between Iressa and Talon that communicates competence through implication; respect for non-Force-sensitive characters' moral weight (Talon, Iressa, Elya, Sela). Benchmark works: Republic Commando series (Hard Contact through Order 66); Imperial Commando: 501st; her Mandalorian texture as a model for institution-as-character.
value.what_to_avoid: Do NOT import Traviss's polemical authorial framing — the drafter must not editorialize about the Jedi Order through the narrator. The investigation IS critical of GAG and the Vigil (by design) but the critique lands through PERSONAL CONSEQUENCE (Elya's dead body, Iressa's lost respectable life, Talon's ruined record) rather than thesis. Do NOT lean on Mandalorian iconography or Mando'a vocabulary — there are no Mandalorians on-page in Book 1.

value.author: Tana French
value.what_to_emulate: NON-STAR-WARS REGISTER SAMPLE. Use exclusively as a sentence-level rhythm reference for Aevyn Soris's precision-with-buried-wound interior register and for Ben's post-PP2 emotional pressure passages. Emulate: controlled, exact interiority that lets the wound surface in fragments rather than confession; long sentences that trail into pause-marked fragments when the speaker brushes the thing they will not say; mystery-genre discipline of revealing only what the POV character can bear to know in this moment. Benchmark works: In the Woods, The Likeness, Broken Harbor.
value.what_to_avoid: Do NOT import French's contemporary urban-Ireland setting register or her police-procedural beats — Aevyn is not a detective and the Force is not a forensic system. Do NOT import French's deliberate withholding of the central explanation (e.g., the Woods conclusion) — Book 1 must resolve its central case cleanly; only the morally dangerous threads stay open. Use French ONLY for sentence-level rhythm in Aevyn's Ch 30 POV and the corridor-flashback fragment, never as a structural model.

claims.value: AEVYN'S CORRIDOR FLASHBACK (preserved verbatim from Planning Bible §17 and Character Voice & Life Sheet v1.4 — the single sharpest character detail in the project; surfaces in Aevyn's Ch 30 POV ONLY as image-fragment, NEVER as exposition, NEVER as speech): Aevyn was at a side console in a working area, running a Recognition exercise Jacen had given him. Jacen was actually present — watching, correcting in real time. It was the longest sustained attention Jacen had given him. Then fourteen-year-old Ben came down the corridor. Jacen looked up, saw the boy, straightened. He said something brief to Aevyn — 'Good. Keep going. We'll review later.' — and walked off with Ben. The 'later' never came. Days passed. When Jacen surfaced again, he picked up where they had left off, gave Aevyn another correction, and acted as though nothing had happened. Because from Jacen's perspective, nothing had happened. He had simply had a thing to do. Aevyn remembers the exact words of the brief dismissal. He remembers Jacen's posture as he turned. He remembers what he was practicing when the moment broke. Ben does not remember Aevyn at all. The wound is not 'Jacen left me' or 'the Jedi rejected me.' The wound is 'Jacen had Ben. I was what he did when Ben wasn't available.' Layered under that: the Jedi rejection at fourteen (a Mid Rim Jedi Knight on a recruiting sweep at a regional outreach office, the forgettable phrase 'we're not able to offer placement at this time'), and GAG dissolving in disgrace after the war — losing his institutional home for the second time.

Talon’s wit can make him seem lighter than he is. The draft must occasionally let the jokes fail.
